newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-THREE SOUTH AFRICANS GIVEN TWO-YEAR DRUGS BANS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-THREE SOUTH AFRICANS GIVEN TWO-YEAR DRUGS BANS.

text.p: South African lock Johan Ackermann and two provincial players have been banned for two years after testing positive for performance enhancing drugs.
A South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) disciplinary commission found Ackermann and Gauteng Lions' players Bennie Nortje and Stefan Bronkhorst had used the anabolic steroid nandrolene.
"I am very happy. Actually I am elated at the decisions," said SARFU chief executive Rian Oberholzer.
"The message is that SARFU will not tolerate drug cheats in the sport.

"I think the finding against Ackermann is especially important to our fight against drug offenders as it shows that no one will be protected. SARFU will not protect a player because of his profile or perceived improtance to the Springbok squad."
Ackermann tested positive during a Springbok training camp in February and had been expected to play an important figure in next month's three test series against the British Lions.
A fourth player has also tested positive and will face a disciplinary hearing later this month.
